review_purpose: Classify R761-R766 by current Main decision relevance; assess novelty, depth, scope, redundancy and provenance limits; provide retrieval briefs so Main need not reopen knowledge-only originals.

main_originals_needed_now.reason: Directly supports the active FP16/BF16 residual, quality and admission decision. Main's review records it was already read; use the existing review and original as needed, with no duplicate reread.
Directly supports active host-copy and queue-call attribution. Main's review records it was already read; use the existing review and original as needed, with no duplicate reread.

reports.retrieval_brief: Concrete five-pass stable GPU grouping for T=8192, K=10, E=512: about 2.65 MB new scratch and explicit ordering/correctness/lifetime rules. Device counts still have to reach the host for the existing oneMKL expert loop, so the design does not remove that synchronization. Consider only if fresh attribution shows route grouping or map return is material.
reports.scope_depth_review: Well bounded and unusually concrete: exact operation/byte budgets, failure checks and an end-to-end comparison plan. Counterevidence includes five launches, local atomic/rank costs and the unchanged host count/order dependency. No material filler; the algorithm is a candidate, not a result.
reports.provenance_limit: Khronos SYCL and Blelloch references plus current fork source; no XeStrata-derived material. Semantics and arithmetic are not B570 performance evidence.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: The 0.16536 s grouping/map-submit interval excludes the prior queue wait and map-copy completion; do not attribute the 167.9548 s explicit-wait CPU time to grouping or infer the wait's cause.

reports.retrieval_brief: Separates mapped host-USM kernel access from explicit queue copies over the same route boundary and proposes a controlled exact-map comparison. It correctly labels bytes as logical payload and keeps the copy-offload safety setting fixed. Use if Main chooses that specific primitive A/B; R765 is the more immediate reference for current residual-copy call internals.
reports.scope_depth_review: Focused comparison with portable SYCL contracts, Intel/Level Zero specifics, NVIDIA/AMD counterexamples and a complete timing/correctness/lifetime plan. Counterevidence is explicit: no B570 transaction, cache or DMA-path evidence; a queue copy is not proven to use dedicated DMA. Some route timing background overlaps other reports but prevents causal overclaiming.
reports.provenance_limit: Primary API/vendor documentation plus explicitly labeled cross-vendor GPU examples; none establishes the current Arc runtime path or a speed result. No XeStrata code or derivatives used.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: Primitive timing and logical byte totals do not establish the full boundary bottleneck; queue waits may drain earlier GPU work.

reports.retrieval_brief: Collects non-LLM database, graph and stencil patterns for fusion, page allocation, device worklists, recomputation and retained dependency state. It adds alternatives and counterexamples beyond generic scan advice, but none proves a Strata bottleneck. Its 75.3 ms transfer floor is arithmetic under a hypothetical 6 GB/s, not measured traffic or removable latency.
reports.scope_depth_review: At the broad edge but held together by avoiding intermediate movement and host roundtrips. Five mechanisms make it a survey rather than a deep comparison; source examples include numeric wins and failures, workload/device caveats and a bounded measurement proposal. No notable filler.
reports.provenance_limit: Primary papers/author material, largely NVIDIA systems and non-LLM workloads. Main's review corrects resource interpretation: 64 MiB scratch alone cannot represent all routed GU/Hh rows; account separately for the approximately 500 MiB full-chunk row materialization and model weights. No XeStrata-derived material.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: Do not treat 451,883,520 logical bytes as PCIe traffic or the 75.3 ms estimate as a speedup bound; host counts/order remain required unless the consumer interface changes.

reports.retrieval_brief: Supports the live FP16/BF16 residual-storage and admission choice. Qwen-family FP8 residual evidence motivates testing but is not a direct FP16/BF16 comparison. The proposed matched FP32/FP16/BF16 screen separates conversion tails, per-context teacher-forced NLL, task outcome and later all-GPU performance; no acceptance threshold is supplied.
reports.scope_depth_review: Substantive and coherent despite a large experimental design: range tails, correlated-token statistics, task scoring, and memory placement are separated. It avoids claiming 16 contexts qualify general quality. The immediate next step is Main's measured screen, not another literature task repeating the absence of direct data.
reports.provenance_limit: Official Qwen report/model README and oneDNN format reference; same-family evidence is not an IQ3 Strata result. Main verified the cited Qwen sections. No measured local format comparison or GPU admission result exists in this report.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: Treat the proposed 16-context sample as a bounded screen; keep quality and performance decisions separate and do not invent a loss margin.

reports.retrieval_brief: Pins a plausible UR v2 batched-queue back-pressure drain in immutable Intel LLVM v7.1.1 source and distinguishes it from normal nonblocking append and explicit pointer import. It proposes ordinary-new[] versus malloc_host timing with idle and prior-work cases. This can explain a host call only conditionally; the captured installed binary and queue mode are not identified.
reports.scope_depth_review: Well bounded, source-specific and falsifiable, with an exact release commit, current-head comparison and a practical measurement matrix. It distinguishes host-call CPU, event wait and full completion. No filler; the key counterevidence is that source describes a possible path, not the current runtime behavior.
reports.provenance_limit: Official Intel source at commit 504366f4b82ff00bbac7b0c956635eed8bc599d8 and separate current-head commit b29c1834fc5795c9748173a1b3ab48e3d75abd28. The release is only the closest source to the v711 label; no binary-to-tag proof, B570 result or PCIe counter is provided.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: A nonblocking API call may drain only on a specific batched-queue limit path; do not infer that Strata used that queue mode. Async return is not proof of a short call or a cached registration.

reports.retrieval_brief: Explains why source SLM or register reductions do not prove occupancy: live-range shortening, rematerialization, unrolling and staged DPAS tiles trade instructions, SLM and concurrent accumulators against compiled GRF/spills and measured kernel time. It gives Intel Max 1550 and AMD MI200 threshold examples and a QSA-specific measurement gate, but no B570 result.
reports.scope_depth_review: Coherent, component-focused and supported by counterexamples where resource reduction does not change occupancy or throughput. It appropriately distinguishes source/requested SLM from compiled static SLM and runtime occupancy. No material filler; the cross-vendor examples must stay illustrative.
reports.provenance_limit: Official Intel GPU/Advisor material and AMD GPUOpen engineering notes; device/compiler/version differ from Arc B570. No code copied or adapted, and no local compiler resource query or measurement was performed.
reports.main_correction_to_retain: Use only if a specific QSA candidate decision needs it and compiled resource fields are available; lower source SLM alone is not an occupancy or speed result.

cross_report_assessment.redundancy: R761 and R762 share route-boundary context but answer distinct questions (stable grouping versus access primitive). R765 is more immediate for residual copy-call internals and should not be merged with R762's mapped-kernel versus explicit-copy comparison. R763 is a broad literature survey but has meaningful mechanisms and counterexamples. R764 and R766 are distinct. No report contains material repeated filler; recurring diagnostic figures serve causal guardrails.
cross_report_assessment.main_read_policy: Use the stored Main reviews for R761-R763 and R766. R764/R765 are decision-relevant originals, already read by Main; do not reread them without a new specific question.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Move variable expert counts from host grouping to an actual device consumer
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: Compare grouped/batched oneMKL calls with host descriptor arrays, bounded expert/tile bucketing, and a device-descriptor consumer for compact MoE. Which alternatives can truly remove the host ne/order dependency, and what are their API, ordering, scratch, launch, load-balance and error-propagation costs?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use official SYCL/oneMKL/Level Zero documentation plus original GPU database or sparse-linear-algebra papers. Include at least two distinct consumer designs and evidence where grouped execution, fusion or device queues fail to remove synchronization or lose to skew/extra work. Relate implications to the 512-expert, top-10, 8192-row chunk without claiming B570 performance.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1200-1600 words; at most 6 substantive primary sources, exact links and an applicability/evidence-limit table. Assign only after Main's full-boundary attribution shows this dependency still matters.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Chunk residency and overlap under a bounded GPU memory budget
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: For repeated long-prefill chunks, compare sequential one-buffer execution, resident-prefix plus one scratch window, and bounded double-buffer overlap. Which dependencies allow useful transfer/compute overlap, and where do queue drain, staging lifetime, memory headroom or synchronization erase it?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use SYCL/Intel primary docs and original non-LLM GPU pipeline studies; compare at least two access/queue schedules and include a case where overlap or extra buffering regresses. Bound capacity arithmetic to the current 8192 chunk and 32768 GPU-resident rows; distinguish design estimates from measurements and include failure/lifetime constraints.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1200-1600 words; at most 6 substantive sources. Do not repeat UR pointer-registration internals from R765 or re-derive R764 storage quality.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Selective residual precision only when errors are localized
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: If Main's R764 screen finds a small number of branches/layers dominate overflow or quality loss, compare fixed per-model dtype, per-layer/per-branch dtype, and sparse higher-precision exception handling. What published evidence supports each, and what storage/dispatch overhead can erase the expected gain?
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use same-family evidence where available plus original activation-compression work; distinguish training quantization, live arithmetic changes and storage-only cast/restore. Include failure cases for outlier handling, correlated quality tests, and task metrics. Do not repeat the generic FP16-versus-BF16 literature gap or introduce an acceptance threshold.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1000-1400 words; at most 6 primary sources. Assign only after the actual per-layer conversion/NLL/task summaries establish that localized exceptions are a live choice.
